Both assembled pages carry the game's own description as body copy (10030-41378 and 10117-44627, the "Slide / Skai Originals" block): "Pick your target and watch the multipliers roll. The carousel slides through multipliers and stops on one, and if it lands at or above the number you called, you get paid. One round, one landing, and everyone's watching the same slide." That is not inference from pixels, it is the designer stating the mechanic. The board render (10030-42256) confirms every clause: a horizontal reel of multiplier cards, each card 110x230 on a 118px pitch, inside a 1413.7px-wide strip positioned at x=-271 within a 954px clipping frame - i.e. an OVERFLOW-HIDDEN reel wider than its viewport, which is what makes it slide; a FIXED WHITE VERTICAL NEEDLE with a ball terminal anchored at the horizontal centre, which the reel travels beneath; the card currently under the needle (6.33x) rendered LARGER than its neighbours (115.7x242 vs 110x230), lifted into a cyan-bordered filled state with a downward chevron notch - the landing card; cards fading out toward both edges via an edge mask; a colour-TIERED cap bar on each card and a matching colour scale in the history strip above (100.92x green, 99.99x and 10.00x amber, 9.99x and 5.00x cyan, 4.99x and 2.00x white, 1.99x neutral), so multiplier magnitude drives colour; and a bottom status bar reading "Participants: 120" behind a live green dot on the left, "Next round in: 4.2s" on the right, over a full-width teal countdown progress bar. SO: SLIDE IS LIMBO'S MATH ON CRASH'S SHARED-ROUND RAILS, PRESENTED AS A CSGO-CASE-OPENING / HORIZONTAL-SPINNER REEL. The player pre-commits a target multiplier before the round; one shared roll resolves for everybody at once; win iff landed >= target; payout at the target, not at the landed value (that is the standard Limbo construction and is the only one consistent with "if it lands AT OR ABOVE the number you called"). NEAREST SIBLING TO FORK: crash/ - and the vocabulary match is not a coincidence, Slide's frame set (Extended LB, Auto, Auto Advanced, LB With Header, Mobile, Mobile Extended LB, Mobile Auto, Mobile Auto Advanced) is a one-for-one reproduction of Crash's page (9137-13564, 9142-16809, 9142-19197, 9142-19454, 9156-1198, 9156-1371, 9156-1558). WHAT DIFFERS FROM CRASH: Crash's multiplier RISES CONTINUOUSLY and the player's decision is WHEN TO CASH OUT mid-round; Slide has no during-round decision at all - the target is locked before the reel moves and there is exactly one landing. That removes the cash-out button, the live rising-multiplier animation, the per-player cashout ledger and the abandoned-round sweep, and replaces them with a single deterministic landing value per round. WHAT DIFFERS FROM instant/: the instant/ games (Dice, Plinko, RPS) are single-player and resolve per-request; Slide has "Participants: 128" and "Next round in: 4.2s", so it needs a shared round lifecycle that instant/ has no machinery for. ||| ★★★ THE APPARENT MECHANIC CONTRADICTION - RAISED, RULED ON, AND RESOLVED 2026-08-19. RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE THE RESOLUTION IS THE USEFUL PART. The two ASSEMBLED pages (10030-41378, 10117-44627) label the field "Target Multiplier:" 2.00; ALL SIX standalone panel variants label the SAME field "Auto Cashout:" 2.00 (10030-42281, 10030-42410, 10030-42517, 10117-46093, 10117-46223, 10117-46330). This lane flagged it as a blocking product decision on the grounds that a cash-out-during-round game and a pre-committed-target game have different risk profiles and different settlement shapes. CASEY RULED: Auto Cashout, i.e. the six panels. ★ AND THE TWO LABELS COLLAPSE RATHER THAN CONFLICT - this lane's "different games" framing was WRONG and is corrected here so nobody re-opens it. Crash's "auto cashout" is NOT a live mid-round action; it is a value the player PRE-SETS and the system exits at automatically when the curve reaches it. So Crash-with-auto-cashout is: win iff crashPoint >= T, pay at T. Limbo is: win iff roll-derived R >= T, pay at T. Those are the same rule. The only thing that distinguishes Crash from Limbo is the OPTION to exit manually mid-round, and a single-landing reel has no continuously-rising value to exit at - the landing is fixed the moment the round is seeded. So the manual branch does not exist in Slide, the two labels denote the same game here, and THE REEL PREMISE SURVIVES INTACT. The panels remain un-relabelled Crash forks, exactly as this lane guessed; the point is that Crash's own label already means "pre-set value", so copying it did not smuggle in a different game. Payout is at the TARGET, not at the landed value, under both readings. ||| ★★★ ODDS AND MULTIPLIERS IN THESE FRAMES ARE DESIGN CONTENT AND ARE NOT A SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR MONEY. Recorded here so nobody mistakes them for a paytable: the reel cards read 1.22x, 1.22x, 1.22x, 1.22x, 10.22x, 5.01x, 6.33x, 1.22x, 2.00x, 102.23x, 1.22x, 1.22x; the history strip reads 1.99x, 1.99x, 1.99x, 1.99x, 100.92x, 99.99x, 10.00x, 9.99x, 5.00x, 4.99x, 2.00x, 1.99x; the panels show "Potential Profit: (4.20x)" alongside a target of 2.00 (internally inconsistent - 4.20x does not follow from 2.00), a balance of "100.11 SKAI / $21.00" on some panels and "100.11 USDC / $1.00" on the desktop page, and 20 identical live-bet rows of "2.340195". The history values are pseudo-pairs (100.92/99.99, 10.00/9.99, 5.00/4.99, 2.00/1.99) - a designer filling a row with plausible-looking numbers, not a sampled distribution - and seven of twelve reel cards being exactly 1.22x is not a Limbo distribution either. ★ THIS IS THE KENO LESSON: Keno's frames were found printing payouts matching no row of the real server table. A frame is a picture of a number, never the number. ALSO ABSENT AND THEREFORE UNSPECIFIED: there is NO house-edge figure and NO RTP anywhere on the page (searched every layer name on the canvas - zero hits for "edge" and "rtp"), where Crash's page states "House Edge 5%" explicitly. There is a "Provably fair" chip and the line "Every game result can be verified using verified" (sic, truncated copy) but NO seed/nonce/verify UI is drawn, so the commit-reveal surface is undesigned. ★★★ RESOLVED 2026-08-19, AND THE NUMBERS NOW COME FROM COMMITTED CODE RATHER THAN FROM A FRAME. Casey ruled per-game STANDARD casino rates (superseding an earlier same-day "align everything to 5%"), and since Slide is Limbo's math the rail is 1%: supabase/functions/_shared/limbo.ts:52 `LIMBO_EDGE_MUL_BPS = 9900`, verified present in this tree, not asserted. THE TARGET BOUNDS ARE THEREFORE DERIVED, NOT INVENTED - limbo.ts:45-46 `LIMBO_MIN_TARGET_BPS = 10100` and `LIMBO_MAX_TARGET_BPS = 10000000`, i.e. 1.01x to 1000x. THIS SUPERSEDES THIS LANE'S EARLIER ADVICE TO REFUSE ANY FLOOR: refusing to invent one was right, but the floor is not a design question at all - it is 1.01x and it already exists. ⚠️ limbo.ts:36-43 warns that FOUR places must agree on these bounds (limbo.ts, gaming_params.go limboMin/MaxTargetBPS, the keeper registry's limbo MinParam/MaxParam, and betParams.ts) because "if one is looser, a bet accepted there is refused elsewhere - the player is charged for a wager that cannot settle". SLIDE WOULD BE A FIFTH CONSUMER and must not widen them. Also note limbo.ts:16-23: RTP = edgeMul/10000 at EVERY target, so picking 1.01x or 1000x changes variance and nothing else - "a change that makes RTP depend on the target has broken limbo rather than tuned it". A reel is a presentation of that same math and must preserve the invariant. ★★★ ONE REAL ENGINEERING GAP FALLS OUT OF THE RULING AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROW: `settleLimbo` (limbo.ts:88-100) RETURNS NO LANDED MULTIPLIER. It returns `{ won, multiplier, payout }` where `multiplier` IS THE TARGET (targetBps/10000), not the landing - Limbo never needs a landed value because it only compares a uniform roll against a threshold. But SLIDE'S ENTIRE VISUAL PREMISE REQUIRES A LANDED VALUE: the reel must stop on a specific card showing a specific number. So Slide is NOT a drop-in reuse of settleLimbo; the landed multiplier must be ADDED, and derived from the SAME `limboRollFromHmac` roll that decides `won` - landedBps = floor(LIMBO_EDGE_MUL_BPS * LIMBO_SCALE / roll), guarding roll = 0 (p = 1e-8). ★ A FIELD NAMED `multiplier` THAT HOLDS THE TARGET IS EXACTLY HOW A UI ENDS UP RENDERING THE WRONG NUMBER ON THE REEL, and if the landing is instead synthesised client-side it will not be the roll that settled the bet - the display/ledger divergence this row warns about, with a concrete mechanism. Range note: minimum possible landing is 0.99x (roll at max), correctly BELOW the 1.01x minimum target since losing landings must exist; the display must reach 1000x. ⚠️ DO NOT INHERIT CRASH'S DISPLAY CAP: crashLiveRoundService.ts:29 pins the displayed multiplier at MAX_MULTIPLIER = 100 while its rail settles uncapped, and Slide's own frames draw a 102.23x card. At 1% edge P(landing >= 100x) = 0.99/100, about 1 round in 101 - not an edge case, roughly 1% of rounds would display a number lower than the one that settled, on day one, if the reel forks Crash's service. ★ COPY THE CROSS-RAIL TEST TOO: limboOdds.test.ts:112-127 reads _shared/limbo.ts's SOURCE and asserts the client constant matches it, failing with "The rail settles at edgeMul X but this panel quotes Y". That is an independent oracle rather than a re-derivation, and it is the cheapest defence against the panel and the rail drifting apart. ||| ⚠ TWO FRAMES ARE DUPLICATED PAGE TEMPLATES NAMED FOR THE WRONG GAME - both are REAL screens with genuine Slide content, and the misleading NAME must not be allowed to corrupt the mechanics read. 10030-41378 is named "Skai > Play > Casino > Towers (1440 x 900px)" and 10117-44627 is named "Skai > Play > Casino > Blackjack (375 x 812px)"; both were duplicated from those games' pages and never renamed. Forking Crash is the right move for the PANEL, the WRONG move for the engine, and - as of the g-shell lane - the wrong move for the PAGE CHROME too. The Crash surface is ~7,950 lines across five files (AviatorGamePro.tsx 5,167, crashLiveRoundService.ts 919, crashMultiplayerService.ts 490, CrashPageSections.tsx 1,111, crashPageContent.ts 262). ★ DO NOT COPY CrashPageSections FOR THE PAGE SCAFFOLD. The title row, fairness sub-bar, section rhythm, page column cap and footer are SHELL, shared by all eleven game pages, and they now exist as components: PlayGamePageShell, PlayGameTitleRow, PlayGameSection, PlayGameSectionDivider, PlayGameSubBarSurface, PlayGamePageFooter from @gaming/components/play/shared, with the measurements and frame ids documented in shared/playPageTemplate.ts. Building the chrome by hand reproduces a fix eleven times and re-imports this frame's reversed title row; it also walks into the two traps that have already caught shipped pages - the fairness sub-bar is 12px = `rounded-lg` (`rounded-xl` is 16px in this app, and nine of ten shipped page files got it wrong), and the title art square is `rounded-[6px]` NOT `rounded-md` (10px here). Reusable near-verbatim FROM CRASH: the entire bet panel including Manual/Auto tabs, 1/2 - 2X - Max chips, the Auto block and the On Win / On Loss / Increase By / Stop on Win / Stop on Loss ladder (Slide's 10030-42517 and 10117-46330 draw these identically to Crash's), the live-bets card, the history strip, and the shared-round lifecycle scaffolding in crashLiveRoundService (countdown, participants count, round open/close). Genuinely NEW and not forkable: the reel component itself - a clipped overflow strip, a deterministic easing curve that must land the correct card exactly under a fixed centre needle, the enlarge/highlight transition on the landing card, the edge fade mask, and the multiplier-to-colour tier scale; plus the server-side round engine (a per-round landing multiplier drawn from a declared distribution, provably-fair commit-reveal, and settlement). ROUGH SIZE: front end ~1.2-2k lines (the chrome is now shell components rather than a fork, the panel is a fork, and the reel is the only real front-end work), server ~400-700 lines, plus the registration tax every game pays - App.tsx route, Play.tsx tile, gameTypeNormalization entry, gameSettlementService type, a `site_config` max-bet row (see the 9-games-frozen-at-defaults finding), a daily-loss-cap row, and a feature flag. ★ THE ANIMATION IS A CORRECTNESS SURFACE, NOT A POLISH SURFACE: the reel must be driven BY the settled result, never the result read off where the animation stopped, or the display and the ledger will disagree exactly the way Crash's 100x display cap already does. ||| QUESTIONS THIS LANE RAISED - FOUR NOW ANSWERED, TWO STILL OPEN. ANSWERED 2026-08-19: (1) Target Multiplier or Auto Cashout - RULED Auto Cashout, and the labels collapse to the same rule anyway; the target is locked before the round and there is no mid-slide exit. (2) Landing distribution and house edge - Limbo's math at a 1% edge, anchored to _shared/limbo.ts:52, with targets bounded 1.01x..1000x by limbo.ts:45-46. (3) Are the reel cards a FIXED finite set or a continuous draw rendered as cards? - CONTINUOUS. Limbo's roll is a uniform integer over LIMBO_SCALE = 1e8 (limbo.ts:61-66), so the landing is drawn from a continuum and the twelve cards are a RENDERING of it, not a wheel the game is built from. This also disposes of the max-win-exposure worry in the old (6): exposure is bounded by LIMBO_MAX_TARGET_BPS = 1000x, because the payout is at the TARGET and the target is what is capped - the landed value can print higher without costing more. STILL OPEN AND WORTH CASEY'S TIME: (A) Shared round or per-player? "Participants: 128" and "everyone's watching the same slide" say shared, and that is materially more infrastructure than Limbo needs - limbo.ts is single-player and carries NO round identity, so the shared-round lifecycle (roundId, participant count, countdown, one landing broadcast to all) is the genuinely new server work and has no existing implementation to fork except Crash's. (B) Which currency rails at launch - the panels disagree between SKAI and USDC, and per the standing gates the sUSD relays and real-money play are separate decisions. NEITHER OF THESE BLOCKS THE REEL OR THE PANEL, so build can proceed ahead of them; (A) blocks the server round engine specifically. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (was `not-started`): re-verified live against the Figma page, the route table and prod site_config. See status.game-rollups.verified.tsv for the evidence.
